core.title: Declare the test's real ATDD phase
core.given: A test file that carries a URN
core.when: you write, bind or edit that test file
core.then: Declare the test's phase with exactly one of RED, UNIT, SMOKE, E2E, using the stack's phase-declaration construct, matching what the test actually does and the proof boundary it exercises.
prefer: Derive the phase from the test's role: RED = current acceptance proof intentionally failing first; UNIT = isolated local behavior; SMOKE = real assembled path/infrastructure with operator-observable evidence; E2E = end-to-end journey through the assembled system.

After declaring, check the test meets what that phase now requires: a RED test must fail first and must assert behaviour; a SMOKE test must assert something operator-observable and must not substitute collaborators. Confirm the phase matches the boundary really exercised.
avoid: Omitting the phase (silently exempts the test from every phase-gated rule).
Choosing a weaker label to silence a phase-gated rule; phase selection is part of the proof contract.
Relabelling a real-path SMOKE or assembled E2E proof as UNIT to permit substitution.
Labelling a passing or vacuous case RED because a RED marker is easy to add.
Inventing a new phase value in an extension; the vocabulary is fixed by core.
unless: The file carries no URN (such files are skipped).
core.why: The phase is not documentation: it selects which other rules apply (e.g. RED must fail first and assert behaviour; SMOKE must assert something operator-observable and must not substitute collaborators), so a perfectly identified test without the right phase is ungoverned or governed by the wrong obligations.
evidence: Every test file carrying a URN has a phase declaration whose value is one of RED, UNIT, SMOKE, E2E, and the stack's convention check reports no finding.

Reviewer confirms the declared phase matches the boundary the case really exercises and that the phase-specific obligations are now evaluated against it: a RED test fails first and asserts behaviour; a SMOKE test asserts something operator-observable and substitutes no collaborators.
verification: Scope: the check applies to every test file of any kind that carries a URN (existing or new; no change-type restriction, no restriction to particular test roles) and reads its phase declaration; files with no URN are skipped. Which files count as test files, and URN carriage itself, are recognized by the stack's checker (URN shapes per the profile's URN keys).
The closed vocabulary RED, UNIT, SMOKE, E2E is fixed by core: any other value or a missing declaration is a finding. Adding a phase is a core change, not an extension change.

A phase-gated rule applies to one phase only; without a declared phase a test is exempt from the whole quality surface by omission, and the phase-gated obligations this field selects (a RED test must fail first and must assert behaviour; a SMOKE test must assert something operator-observable and must not substitute collaborators) cannot be evaluated.
The mechanical check covers only presence and vocabulary of the declaration; whether the declared phase matches the role and proof boundary actually exercised is judged by review, not by the check.
Severity 2; disposition strict: the realization fails on every finding, with no advisory mode and no ratchet baseline.

values: declared phase value outside RED, UNIT, SMOKE, E2E
declared phase does not match the role/proof boundary exercised

fires: A test file carrying a URN has no phase declaration.
A test file carrying a URN declares a phase with a value outside RED, UNIT, SMOKE, E2E.
A test file carrying a URN that exercises the real assembled path is labelled UNIT so that collaborator substitution is permitted.
A test file carrying a URN labels a passing or vacuous case RED only because a RED marker is easy to add.
doesNotFire: A test file with no URN (skipped by this rule).
A test file carrying a URN whose declared phase is one of RED, UNIT, SMOKE, E2E and matches the role and proof boundary the test actually exercises.

profileRequirements.meaning: The construct by which a test file declares its ATDD phase (field name, placement and value syntax); the core's 'declare the phase' obligation targets this construct, and the activation findings 'phase declaration missing' and 'value outside the vocabulary' are evaluated against it.
profileRequirements.bunValue: `// Phase:` with RED, UNIT, SMOKE or E2E

neutralityNotes: bun.json itself declares this a stack-neutral obligation with a Bun-specific detector, so almost everything is core: the phase vocabulary RED/UNIT/SMOKE/E2E stays in the core because bun.json fixes it at core level ('adding a phase is a core change'), and per-rule severity and disposition stay in core verification. The Bun activation kind 'test' is kept unrestricted in the core (file_kind: test, with doesNotFire limited to non-test files): the closed role vocabulary's three test roles (unit_test, acceptance_test, e2e_test) do not exhaust Bun's scope — a smoke or integration test carrying a URN is in scope — so no renaming to those roles is made; recognizing which files count as test files is owned by the stack's realization, matching bun.json's own deferral to its detector, and no profileRequirement is fabricated for it because bun.json states no concrete test-file recognition values. Similarly, URN shapes/bindings are deferred to the profile's URN keys without fabricated values. Only two things are Bun-specific: the concrete declaration construct `// Phase:` (carried by the proposed profile key idiom.test_constructs#phase_declaration, since no existing key covers a named declaration field beyond comment syntax or URN bindings) and the detector id bun_tester_discipline_detector (bunOnly; the core names the check generically).
